name: Rhododendron forests, thickets and heaths
status: 5 archetypal species (full list archived in docs/plant_archive)
notes: Over 1,000 species exist; these form landscapes: Himalayan red forests, Appalachian hells and balds, Black Sea understory, alpenrose heath, Siberian dahurica, Yunnan giants, arctic dwarfs, tropical epiphytic vireyas. Bee- and bird-pollinated; nectar toxic (mad honey). Acid soil: peat and granite, absent on limestone.

canopy.name: Tree rhododendron

growth.juvenile_note: Dust-fine seeds sprout on moss or mossy banks: two minute round cotyledons, then tiny hairy leaves. For years it is a small, slow sapling, each year's shoot ending in a tuft of long, leathery, dark green leaves, silvery to rusty-felted beneath; later one or a few stems lead and it becomes a tree with rough, peeling reddish-brown bark.
growth.source: Wikipedia Rhododendron arboreum (usually 12 m, to 20 m; leaves 7-19 cm; trusses of 15-20 bell-shaped flowers 5 cm wide, red, pink or white); growth, ages and seedling habits estimated from Himalayan forest ecology and horticultural experience with tree rhododendrons

canopy.source: Himalaya and S Indian hills; forest-forming; Blood-red blossom forests of Nepal and Sikkim. Kew POWO; standard floras.

canopy.name: Big-leaf rhododendron

growth.juvenile_note: Young plants carry the biggest leaves of any rhododendron (up to 70-90 cm long), glossy dark green above with silvery-buff felt beneath, held in a loose rosette at the top of a stout, sparsely branched stem. Leaves get smaller as the plant ages and starts to flower; seedlings start tiny on moss and need shelter, humidity and part shade.
growth.source: Wikipedia Rhododendron sinogrande (tree to 12 m; leaves up to 70 cm, occasionally 90 x 35 cm; flowers up to 8 cm, late spring; 2,100-3,600 m); larger leaves on young plants, slow flowering (15+ yr from seed) and growth rates from horticultural experience (estimated)

canopy.source: Yunnan-Burma cloud forest; Leaves to a metre long. Kew POWO; standard floras.

shrub.name: Great rhododendron

growth.juvenile_note: Seeds sprout on moss, rotting logs or bare wet soil; the seedlings are tiny and grow very slowly for years. The young plant is a thin sprig bearing whorls of long, dark green, leathery leaves at the tip of each year's shoot; it gains 15-20 cm a year in light shade and spreads by layering into dense, tangled 'laurel hell' thickets.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Rhododendron maximum (seeds can germinate as soon as shed, need light; 92-97% after 21 days; terminal growth 15-20 cm per season in lighter shade; seedlings grow best in partial shade but survive deep shade; stems may reach 100 yr; up to 12 m); first flowering estimated

shrub.source: Appalachian coves and stream banks; Rhododendron hells under hemlock. Kew POWO; standard floras.

shrub.name: Alpenrose

growth.juvenile_note: Minute seedlings on moss or raw humus: two tiny cotyledons, then small glossy, dark green, leathery leaves with rusty-brown scaly undersides and rolled edges. For years it is a small, few-stemmed sprig; then it branches densely into a low, rounded evergreen bush, and stems that touch the ground root and spread it into a clonal patch.
growth.source: German Wikipedia Rostblaettrige Alpenrose (30-130 cm; stems 1-2 cm thick nearly 100 yr old; leaves live ~2 yr; flowers May-Jul, corolla to 2 cm, deep pink to red; capsules to 7 mm ripen from August; semi-shade light value; 440-2,840 m); germination and first flowering estimated

epiphyte.name: Vireya rhododendron

growth.juvenile_note: Vireya seeds carry a thread-like tail at each end and lodge in moss on branches or banks. The seedling is a tiny sprig of small, scaly, elliptic leaves; it grows in quick flushes, each ending in a whorl of glossy, leathery leaves, and becomes a loose, straggly, few-stemmed shrub perched on a mossy branch or rooted in the ground.
growth.source: Wikipedia Rhododendron javanicum (evergreen shrub to 5 m, terrestrial or epiphytic; bright orange spring flowers; Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines); germination, growth and first flowering estimated from vireya growers' experience (seedlings flower in about 2-4 years)
